Quantify the home range using local convex hulls (LoCoH)

Source: R/hr_tt_locoh.R
hr_tt_locoh.Rd

This function estimates the home range of an animal using the local convex hull (LoCoH) method of Getz & Wilmers (2004) and Getz et al. (2007). A convex hull is built around each location and a set of its neighbours; the hulls are then sorted from the smallest to the largest, and the home range for a given level is the union of the smallest hulls that, between them, contain that proportion of the locations. Unlike the minimum convex polygon (hr_tt_mcp()), LoCoH home ranges can have several parts, holes and concave edges, so they can exclude areas that are never visited.

Usage

hr_tt_locoh(
  x,
  n = 10,
  type = c("k", "r", "a"),
  levels = c(0.5, 0.95),
  buffer = 0
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object; if explicitly grouped, the home range is estimated for each group, combining all tracks within each group. Otherwise, the track id is used as grouping variable. Every group must have events, so groupings with empty groups (e.g. from grouping by a factor with unused levels with .drop = FALSE) give an error.

n

The parameter of the LoCoH, whose meaning depends on type: the number of nearest neighbours for "k" (a whole number of at least 2), the radius for "r", or the maximum sum of the distances for "a" (both in the units of the projection of x). Either a single value, or a vector with one value per group, matched to the groups in the order of dplyr::group_keys() (i.e. sorted by the grouping variables).

type

The type of LoCoH: "k" (the default), "r" or "a" (see Details).

levels

A vector of levels (proportions of locations) for the home ranges, as numbers between 0 and 1. The default is c(0.5, 0.95), which corresponds to the 50% and 95% home ranges.

buffer

A non-negative number: the distance (in the units of the projection of x) by which the home ranges are buffered. The default, 0, leaves them as they are; a small positive value (e.g. 1e-5, as in amt::hr_locoh()) also includes the hulls with no area (see Details).

Value

An sf tibble of subclass hr_tt_poly_tbl of results, with one row per group and level, and columns:

  • the grouping variable (as named in x; if x is grouped by multiple variables, this column is named group_id): the ids from the grouping of x

  • method: the method used to estimate the home range ("locoh")

  • type: the type of LoCoH ("k", "r" or "a")

  • n: the parameter of the LoCoH

  • level: the level of the home range

  • area: the area of the home range (as computed by sf::st_area())

  • geometry: the geometry of the home range as sf multipolygons

Details

Events with an empty geometry (i.e. no location) are ignored.

Three ways of choosing the neighbours of each location are available, depending on type:

  • "k" (fixed number of neighbours): each hull is built from a location and its n nearest neighbours. Note that adehabitatHR::LoCoH.k() uses k - 1 neighbours, so n = k - 1 gives the same hulls.

  • "r" (fixed radius): each hull is built from all the locations within a distance n of a location.

  • "a" (adaptive): each hull is built from the locations closest to a location such that the sum of their distances to it is at most n. Getz et al. (2007) suggest using the largest distance between any two locations as a starting value for n.

The neighbour search, the hulls, their areas and the number of hulls needed for each level are computed in C++ (with a k-d tree for the neighbour search); the union of the hulls is computed with sf::st_union().

The rules follow amt::hr_locoh(): each level is matched to the union of hulls whose coverage (the proportion of locations in the hulls) is closest to it, so the actual coverage can be a little above or below the requested level. A hull with no area (when all its locations lie on a line, or are at the same place, as it may be the case for locations at the den or nest) counts towards the coverage, but only becomes part of the isopleth if buffer is positive. amt::hr_locoh() buffers every hull by 1e-5 (its rand_buffer); setting buffer = 1e-5 here gives the same isopleths.

Distances are computed in the units of the projection of x, and hulls are built and merged on a plane. For unprojected data (longitude/latitude), distances (and so n for types "r" and "a", and buffer) are thus in degrees, and the hulls are distorted (increasingly so away from the equator); it is recommended to project x to an appropriate projection before using this function. Areas are computed with sf::st_area(), in the units of the projection of x (e.g. m^2 for a UTM projection), or in m^2 for unprojected data.

References

Getz, W. M., & Wilmers, C. C. (2004). A local nearest-neighbor convex-hull construction of home ranges and utilization distributions. Ecography, 27(4), 489-505.

Getz, W. M., Fortmann-Roe, S., Cross, P. C., Lyons, A. J., Ryan, S. J., & Wilmers, C. C. (2007). LoCoH: nonparameteric kernel methods for constructing home ranges and utilization distributions. PLoS ONE, 2(2), e207.

Examples

# the tracks in example_tt are short (5 locations each), so each hull is
# built from a location and its 3 nearest neighbours
example_locoh <- hr_tt_locoh(example_tt, n = 3)
example_locoh
